mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Damaging wind potential continues within WW547.

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A bowing segment continues eastward across northern Indiana, with recent wind gusts to 67 mph reported near Fort Wayne, IN. KIWX radar continues to sample winds around 60 kts around 2 kft. Initial outflow has rushed out ahead of the main line, with additional thunderstorm development ongoing ahead of the line near the outflow. Storms have become better oriented with the mean flow/deep layer shear, which may help aid downstream organization. The greater buoyancy is located across southern/central Ohio. It seems most likely that the southern portion of the line will continue to evolve along this gradient into portions of Ohio with continued damaging wind gusts 60-70 mph downstream for the next couple of hours before outrunning better buoyancy.

mesoscaleDiscussions.summary: Isolated to widely scattered thunderstorms will likely spread across southern Arizona through the late afternoon/evening hours. Watch issuance is not anticipated given the fairly modest kinematic environment, though a few severe downbursts appear possible.

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Latest GOES imagery and lightning data show the onset of deep convection both along the Mogollon Rim and within the higher terrain of southern/southeast AZ. Although this activity has been slow to move off the terrain so far, modest easterly flow through much of the column, combined with cold-pool propagation, should promote thunderstorms spreading westward over the next several hours. As this occurs, convection will begin to impinge on a very deeply mixed, but buoyant, air mass characterized by MLCAPE values of around 500-1000 J/kg and 40-45 F dewpoint depressions (which suggest LCL heights are around 3 to 3.5 km). This thermodynamic profile is very conducive for accelerating downdrafts capable of producing swaths of strong to severe winds (possibly as high as 55-70 mph) within the more intense downbursts. Although a favorable thermodynamic environment is in place, the observed wind profiles from regional VWPs show meager deep-layer wind shear with 0-6 km BWD values of around 15 knots - somewhat weaker than the 20-25 knots depicted by RAP mesoanalyses and recent HRRR solutions. Consequently, the expectation is for sporadic strong to severe downburst winds within poorly organized cells and clusters through at least early evening. This activity should remain sufficiently transient and isolated to preclude the need for a watch.
